parsed.explanation: Combined regime: national entry screening (Feb 2025 cable) refuses applicants on any sex-document discrepancy and flags possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; passport sex markers are now birth-sex only, with some travellers stranded. Immigration custody shows documented forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse of trans men. The state adds a facilities law with a documented trespass arrest and 24 hours held in a men's ward, plus birth-certificate marker bans, a care ban under 18, and no state gender-identity hate-crime or public-accommodation protection. Mitigations are real but thin: national employment and hate-crime law, and a national hate-crime statute. Lethal outcomes and imprisonment are not documented. Severity is high and exposure is recurring, so the rating falls in the High Risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport sex markers now birth-sex only; X markers stopped for new issue. Entry cable directs refusal on any document discrepancy and requests further evidence. Lifetime fraud ineligibility is possible though never automatic. Advisories from allied governments followed detentions of their citizens.
entry_documents.protection: Documented: existing X passports remain valid until expiry; a challenge is pending in national courts. Documented: a legal-aid FAQ exists. No operative visitor-facing protection documented.
entry_documents.interaction: A discrepancy at entry can lead to refusal, requests for evidence, and a possible fraud finding that bars future entry. Passport blocking can leave travellers stranded.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Federal custody policy adopted from one state's model mandates conversion-style treatment and removal of hormones; the bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner counts from 2025. Facilities-trespass arrest with handcuffing and 24 hours in a men's ward documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Documented: release on pretrial bail after the trespass arrest. Documented: no conviction or imprisonment for the single facilities case in the record.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody placement by birth sex plus documented abuse within detention means a detained visitor faces severe harm. Facilities trespass requires refusal to leave, but the arrest shows enforcement reaches visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facilities bans by gender identity in all government buildings in 9 states plus one more, covering K-12 and colleges; bans in some government buildings in 9 further states; schools-only bans in 3. In 6 states bans reach some private settings. Four states criminalise bathroom use in some circumstances. Visitors are reached through state-owned buildings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The state in the division has no facilities ban at the parent-rule level beyond the 2025 law's scope, and its statute carries exemptions. No documented operative protection in this state for facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The combined regime applies the national facilities climate, the 2025 state law covering state-owned buildings and colleges, and the trespass offence. Reasonable-accommodation wording is unresolved and may lead to solitary confinement.

care_services.exposure: State ban on gender-affirming care under 18 (2023). Proposed national rules to bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18s. National subpoenas of over 20 hospitals for full records of under-19 patients. Documented denial of care in custody. National crisis lifeline youth services closed.
care_services.protection: Documented: the state's 2024 settlement with a health-advocacy organisation included an apology and a non-discrimination commitment, though it was about contracting, not trans visitors' care.
care_services.interaction: A minor seeking care faces state prohibition and possible federal records access, and a clinic may disclose patient records. Adult care access for visitors is not documented as restricted by state law here.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as a target for neutralisation. December 2025 cash-reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology' as a marker of extremism. State gender-marker bans on birth certificates. Official rhetoric describes trans people as a threat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Documented: the counterterrorism strategy states powers will not target people who merely disagree. Some national courts have enjoined orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level threat framing and national security framing can reach trans advocates and possibly visitors who take part in advocacy. The disclaimer is not an operative safeguard.

minors_guardians.exposure: Criminal exposure for teachers who facilitate social transition of a minor; investigation of schools; state ban on care under 18; national subpoenas of hospital records. A travelling minor's guardian risks investigation tied to care or school contact.
minors_guardians.protection: Documented: some national orders are blocked or enjoined. Protection for visiting minors is not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's care or school contact can bring the guardian into a federal or state investigation. Records-based exposure may reach beyond the visit.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Gender-identity hate crimes covered federally; 37 states lacked anti-bias gender-identity statutes as of 2019. Bias against sexual orientation accounts for a large share of incidents; no trans-specific violence rate documented. Police response to trans victims is not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and national employment protection apply. Twenty-two states plus the capital district prohibit gender-identity discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The state in the division has no gender-identity hate-crime or public-accommodation law, so the national backstop is the only recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Most orders are contested and change with litigation. State rules on driver's licence marker change are unclear after the March 2026 ruling. Enforcement of reasonable accommodation in state custody is unresolved. Trespass charges require refusal to leave, but enforcement of that standard is unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented: a national civil-liberties suit, pretrial release, and a 2024 state settlement showing recourse can work. Documented: some national orders are enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is slow and uneven, so traveller exposure follows whichever measures are in force on the day of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: entry refusal and discretionary exclusion of visibly trans visitors without imprisonment. Lower in part: this dossier also documents immigration-custody beatings and sexual abuse, lifetime fraud ineligibility, and a state facilities arrest. Anchor 0.35-A has no documented custodial harm, so the case sits somewhat below it.

Similar: birth-sex custody placement with assaults, criminalised bathroom use, and documented custodial harm. Higher in part: the 0.25-C anchor adds a criminal cross-dressing statute and frequent raids, whereas here the facilities offence requires refusal to leave and no raids are documented. Roughly comparable, slightly higher.

Lower: 0.15-B has detention for entry, crowded cells, guard-permitted assaults, and capital-penalty provisions. This dossier documents custodial abuse but no capital pathway and no routine detention of visitors for presentation. It sits clearly above 0.15-B.

parsed.synthesis: Traveller-facing exposures are documented at several levels. Entry screening refuses on document discrepancy and may impose lifetime fraud ineligibility. Immigration custody shows serious abuse. The state adds a facilities regime with one documented trespass arrest, a care ban for minors, and no state gender-identity protections. National measures add threat framing and records access. Mitigations exist but are partial: national hate-crime and employment law, enjoined orders, and one state settlement. No capital or imprisonment pathway is documented, so severity is high but not at the extreme. The combined regime sits in the High Risk band.
